newsitem.title: USA: Foreign crude business to US eyes weakening Brent.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crude business to US eyes weakening Brent.

text.p: Foreign crude business to the U.S. focused on the weakening Dated Brent market, where deals were done at ever-cheapening prices on Monday.
A pair of wet deals saw two late March dates move, the first for Mar 27-29 at April Brent -80 cents and then for Mar 26-28 at April Brent -81 cts.
"On the wet side there were really only those two deals to speak of," said a Brent trader, who noted the sluggish pace of business.
Traders said the soft tone for Brent should put the pressure on U.S. domestic sweet barrels, considering the arbitrage window has also played into more trans-Atlantic shipments.
Despite some modest gains for the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James on Monday, the outlook is for more Brents coming over in the near future.

"Why wouldn't somebody try with these numbers in place. You're looking at the arbitrage at around $1.25 for April West Texas Intermediate/Brent, and the dated 80 cents under April Brent," said a crude trader.
Other markets were quiet, with Latin American traders noting the weakness in most grades continued. Reductions in Colombian Cusiana and Cano Limon prices were reflective of the trend, traders said.
An unconfirmed deal for Cano Limon put the crude's value at WTI minus $3.10, with the Cusiana pegged around a discount of 80 cents to $1.00, sources said.

U.S. aftermarket dealings moved Brent paper values lower, but only around 600 lots changed hands in May Brent outrights. A trio of inter-month April/May spreads were done at +14/15 cts, steady with earlier clockings.
